title: Create and manage multiple wallets
body:
Multiple wallets can be useful for many reasons...

It can be used to separate different types/purposes/uses/etc.
(e.g. "readily available" amounts vs "set aside for holding, staking, etc")

And...
spreading assets across more than one wallet becomes an additional "safety buffer," in that if one of the wallets gets compromised somehow, only a portion of your holdings would be at risk

Possible requirement: Additional recovery tags(?)

title: Add a feature to track active recovery tags, show which backs up the wallet, and how many are used.
body:
If a wallet allows multiple recovery tags (for example, 3 recovery tags), how can we verify which one is actually linked as a backup to the wallet?

How should recovery tags be properly managed - are they stored on the phone, on the Ryder hardware wallet, or both?

Currently, there's no clear way to track how many recovery tags have already been created or used. It would be very helpful to add a feature that shows:

- How many recovery tags are active
- Which one is linked to the wallet backup
- The status of each recovery tag

This would improve transparency, security, and overall user experience.

comments.body: This is the same confusion situation im facing! Please do it soon...
100% agree this is what ryder should be leading towards if they said recovery and cold wallet is their priority as hardware, this features is a must.

title: Support for sbtc
body:
As a big fan of Ryder's super simple, secure hardware wallet (especially with its deep Stacks roots and role in Nakamoto signers), I'd love to see sBTC added as a supported asset.

sBTC is the trustless, non-custodial 1:1 Bitcoin-backed asset on Stacks that finally unlocks real BTC for DeFi, lending, yield farming, and dApps - without ever selling your Bitcoin or relying on centralized custodians.

Adding sBTC support in Ryder would help the Stacks ecosystem by:

- Making it easier and more secure for Bitcoin holders to safely move BTC to sBTC to Stacks apps (and back) using a top-tier hardware wallet.
- Driving more adoption and liquidity into Stacks DeFi, as users could hold/manage/programmable Bitcoin directly in their Ryder wallet with offline security.
- Unlocking over $1T in dormant Bitcoin capital for productive use on the leading Bitcoin L2, boosting the entire Bitcoin + Stacks economy.
- Aligning perfectly with Ryder's Bitcoin focus (like FAST Pool, Nakamoto participation, and future sBTC payouts) and making self-custody even more seamless for the community.

This would be a game-changer for secure, user-friendly access to Bitcoin-native DeFi. What do you think - any plans or interest in adding sBTC?

Thanks for building such an awesome product!
